results.claim: The literal optimized algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M), where M=Σ_t d(p_t) along its actual FIFO trajectory, but the ordered queue is part of the state.
results.proof_sketch: Let p_t be the shelf and q_t=(x_1,…,x_k) the current FIFO queue. Initialization puts the left-to-right descent bottoms in q_0. A local adjacency induction using the pseudocode’s two enqueue tests shows that, at every round boundary, q_t contains exactly the descent bottoms D(p_t) as a set, although not necessarily in shelf order. Processing q_t yields p_{t+1}=reverse(q_t) followed by the elements outside q_t in their previous relative order. Hence |q_t|=d(p_t) and M is the total number of queue pops. The initial scan costs Θ(n), and every pop performs Θ(1) pointer and queue work. The queue’s order is history-dependent, so p_{t+1}=reverse(D(p_t)) followed by U(p_t) is not a valid autonomous transition.

results.claim: For every m≥3, the literal FIFO algorithm on A_m=(1,2m,2,2m−1,…,m,m+1) makes exactly (m²+5m−4)/2 moves in m+2 rounds.
results.proof_sketch: Write S for the shelf and Q for the ordered queue. Initially Q_0=(2,…,m). When j∈Q_0 is processed, its predecessor and successor are 2m+2−j and 2m+1−j, so the successor test enqueues 2m+1−j; the current front j−1 is then enqueued by the front test. Hence S_1=(m,…,1,2m,…,m+1) and Q_1=(2m−1,1,2m−2,2,…,m+1,m−1). In Q_1, a high entry has no qualifying successor (the next high is smaller than it), and a low entry’s successor exceeds its predecessor. The first high enqueues front m, and each later high enqueues the preceding low, giving S_2=(m−1,m+1,m−2,m+2,…,1,2m−1,m,2m), Q_2=(m,1,…,m−2). Processing Q_2 similarly gives, with a=m−2, S(a)=(a,a−1,…,1,a+2,a+1,a+3,…,2m), Q(a)=(a+1,1,2,…,a−1). Here and below shelves follow from S^+=reverse(Q)·U(S). For every a≥2, processing Q(a) enqueues a from the first front test, then 1,…,a−2 from later front tests; every successor test is false because the relevant successor exceeds its predecessor. Thus (S(a),Q(a)) maps to (S(a−1),Q(a−1)). At a=1, Q=(2) produces (2,1,3,…,2m), Q=(1), and the last move sorts. Queue sizes are m−1,2m−2,m−1,m−2,…,1,1; they sum to (m²+5m−4)/2 and give m+2 rounds.

results.claim: The worst-case step complexity of the literal optimized algorithm is Ω(n²).
results.proof_sketch: For n=2m, the preceding exact count is n²/8+5n/4−2. For n=2m+1, append the new maximum 2m+1 to A_m. It creates no initial descent, is never queued, and leaves every prefix operation unchanged. In particular, whenever it supplies a successor where the even instance had no successor, the successor test is false because the new maximum cannot be smaller than the predecessor. Hence the odd instance has the same move count. Every move entails at least one unit operation, so for every sufficiently large n the worst-case cost is at least (⌊n/2⌋²+5⌊n/2⌋−4)/2=Ω(n²).

results.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
results.proof_sketch: Let i be the largest unfixed value and let s_i<i be its position when its phase begins. Every larger value belongs to a permanent fixed suffix, so i is never marked. In a round, moving an element that began left of i shifts i left on removal and right on prepending, for net zero. Moving one that began right of i shifts i right exactly once. If q_t and ℓ_t count the moved elements respectively right and left of i, then i advances by q_t. Consequently Σ_t q_t=i−s_i over the phase, and its exact move cost is (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t. This is independent of the FIFO processing order.

results.claim: The parent’s Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound and coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)) are not established for the literal optimized FIFO algorithm.
results.proof_sketch: The staircase recurrence describes the ordinary shelf-ordered transition, not the persistent FIFO queue. For P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), after three rounds the ordinary transition has state (3,1,2,6,4,5), whereas the literal optimized pseudocode has (1,3,2,6,4,5). Thus the claimed prefix identity already fails at this finite boundary, and its subsequent summation cannot supply a lower bound for the target algorithm.

results.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
results.proof_sketch: All 409,113 permutations of sizes 1 through 9 were exhaustively executed under the literal FIFO pseudocode. Three implementations—vector-based, std::list-based, and a value-indexed predecessor/successor array—agreed on every queue, boundary state, round count, and move total. The maxima were attained and no enumerated permutation exceeded them.

results.claim: For every m≥2, the canonical boundary-descent-pair charging rule has unbounded load: on B_m=(2,1,4,3,…,2m,2m−1), the single pair {1,3} is charged at least m−1 times.
results.proof_sketch: Charge a move of x to {x,y}, where y is x’s predecessor at the start of that round; y>x because x is then a descent bottom. The cases m=2,3 are direct. For m≥4, initialization on B_m has Q_0=(1,3,…,2m−1). Processing it gives S_1=(2m−1,2m−3,…,1,2,4,…,2m) and Q_1=(1,3,…,2m−3). Put L_0=Q_0 and, for 1≤r≤m−1, L_r=(1,3,…,2m−2r−1), with L_{m−1}=(1). Inductively Q_r=P_rL_r and S_r begins with reverse(L_{r−1}). The r=1,2 transitions give P_2=(2), P_3=(4). From r=3 onward, just before L_r is processed, the element c_r after 1 is alternately 2 or 4. Processing L_r makes the last element of P_{r+1} equal c_r: if c_r=2 it is enqueued while removing 1; if c_r=4 it is enqueued immediately before the front-generated 1. That last prefix element is moved immediately before 1 next round and is not re-enqueued by the remaining odd suffix, so c_{r+2}=c_r. For odd x≥5, c_r is never strictly between x and its predecessor x+2, so its successor test is false; the front tests on 3,5,… append 1,3,… and give suffix L_{r+1}. Thus the induction closes. For every r=1,…,m−1, reverse(L_{r−1}) contains adjacent 3,1 and Q_r contains 1. Hence 1 is charged to {1,3} in m−1 distinct rounds, ruling out every constant load for this canonical charge.

results.claim: Even with arbitrary reassignment of moves to unordered pairs, a uniform pair capacity must be at least 19 on one 4096-element execution.
results.proof_sketch: For B_{2048}=(2,1,4,3,…,4096,4095), two independent literal-FIFO implementations both count 156,213,604 moves in 130,514 rounds. There are binom(4096,2)=8,386,560 unordered pairs. A scheme assigning every move to exactly one pair with capacity 18 could cover at most 18·8,386,560=150,958,080 moves, which is 5,255,524 too few. Therefore its uniform integral capacity is at least ceil(156,213,604/8,386,560)=19. This subsumes the parent’s capacity-two counterexample, but it is deliberately only a finite obstruction and proves no superquadratic asymptotic lower bound.

results.claim: No asymptotically tight worst-case bound is proved here; the improved Ω(n²)–O(n³) interval remains unresolved.
results.proof_sketch: The audited arbitrary-size family proves Ω(n²), while the source’s O(n³) upper bound still applies. The new B_m induction rules out any constant-capacity proof based on charging each move to its round-boundary descent pair, but that is an obstruction to a proof method rather than a larger move lower bound. The capacity-19 result is finite and likewise has no asymptotic consequence. The phase identity still leaves its left-of-active term uncontrolled. Thus there is still neither an O(n²) upper bound nor an Ω(n³) construction or any other matching pair of bounds, so the requested tight asymptotics remain open.

final_writeup:
Resolution status: PARTIAL. The literal optimized FIFO algorithm still has only a proved Ω(n²)–O(n³) worst-case interval. This attempt strengthens the obstruction to a natural pair-charging proof, but it does not close that interval.

At a round boundary the state is the shelf p together with the ordered FIFO queue Q. The queue contains exactly the descent bottoms D(p) as a set, but its order is history-dependent. Processing Q gives reverse(Q) followed by the unqueued elements in stable order, while the two local tests construct the next ordered queue. Thus the running time is Θ(n+M), where M is the total number of queue pops, equivalently the sum of descent counts along the actual FIFO trajectory. A shelf alone does not determine its successor.

The audited quadratic family remains unchanged. For m≥3,

A_m=(1,2m,2,2m−1,…,m,m+1)

has queue-size sequence

m−1, 2m−2, m−1, m−2, …, 1, 1.

The literal successor and front tests give exactly (m²+5m−4)/2 moves in m+2 rounds. With n=2m this is n²/8+5n/4−2, and appending a new maximum preserves the trajectory for odd sizes. Hence the worst-case step complexity is Ω(n²).

The new obstruction uses the adjacent-swap family

B_m=(2,1,4,3,…,2m,2m−1).

Consider the canonical local charge that assigns each moved descent bottom x to the unordered pair consisting of x and its predecessor at the start of that round. Initialization has Q_0=(1,3,…,2m−1), and the first round produces

S_1=(2m−1,2m−3,…,3,1,2,4,…,2m),
Q_1=(1,3,…,2m−3).

For 1≤r≤m−1 let L_r=(1,3,…,2m−2r−1), ending with L_{m−1}=(1). Induction through the literal tests writes Q_r=P_rL_r and makes S_r begin with reverse(L_{r−1}). The first two transitions give P_2=(2) and P_3=(4). Thereafter the element exposed after 1 while the odd suffix is processed alternates between 2 and 4: processing the suffix makes that gate the last element of P_{r+1}; it is moved immediately before 1 next round and is not re-enqueued by the remaining suffix. This gives the two-step recurrence for the gate. No successor test on an odd x≥5 succeeds, while the front tests regenerate L_{r+1}. Therefore S_r contains adjacent 3,1 and Q_r contains 1 for every r=1,…,m−1. The same pair {1,3} receives at least m−1 charges. Consequently no constant capacity per pair can prove an upper bound via this canonical boundary-descent charge. This is an asymptotic obstruction to that method, not a superquadratic move lower bound.

A separate finite check shows the limitation persists even if charges may be assigned arbitrarily rather than to their witnessing descents. The 4096-element instance B_{2048} makes exactly 156,213,604 moves. Since 18·binom(4096,2)=150,958,080, any assignment of every move to one unordered pair needs uniform integral capacity at least 19 on this execution. This strengthens the parent’s capacity-two witness, but a single finite instance has no asymptotic force.

The phase decomposition remains the unresolved bottleneck. During the phase of the largest unfixed value i, moves originating to its right advance i once, whereas moves originating to its left have zero net positional effect. If the phase begins at position s_i, its exact cost is (i−s_i) plus the number of left-of-i moves; no sufficiently sharp bound on the latter is known here. The earlier Ω(n^{3/2}) staircase argument still fails because it replaces persistent FIFO order by current shelf order, already diverging on P_6. Exact maxima through n=9 remain 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.

Accordingly, this is material method-level progress only. No O(n²) upper bound, Ω(n³) construction, or other matching pair of bounds is established, so the requested asymptotically tight complexity is not solved.
